clue.text: Carriage for one in drive

indicators.note: in tells us the word for one sits inside the word for drive

parts.note: to drive game out of cover is to chase it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A request for a vehicle with room for just one passenger out on a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' wants to be a car outing; it is CHASE, as in driving or hunting game. 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaise is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle, often seating only one or two.

clue.text: Sticking together, he has joined firm, and I have too

indicators.note: joined says the next pieces are attached to the word for firm, in sequence

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm
he has contracts to he's
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone describes staying loyal: he has joined a company and so have I.
explanation.walkthrough: The contractions he's and I've lose their apostrophes when they go into the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cohesive holds together as a unit, its parts adhering to one another.

clue.text: Highest post available for foreign correspondent

definitions.text: Highest post available for foreign correspondent

parts.words: Highest post available for foreign correspondent
parts.note: the post that travels highest, flown overseas, is the service used by anyone writing letters abroad

explanation.surface: The top job open to a reporter stationed overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' and 'foreign correspondent' suggest a journalist's career; read instead as letters sent overseas by plane, the highest-flying mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters to correspondents abroad are carried by aircraft, the post that travels at the greatest height.

clue.text: Unable to answer question at university, paid the price?

parts.note: someone baffled by a question is stumped
UP means in residence at university, as in going up to Oxford

explanation.surface: A student who could not answer an exam question and suffered for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'paid the price' is meant literally: to stump up is to pay what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumping up is British slang for handing over money, reluctantly paying a bill.

clue.text: One top detective is a drug user

parts.note: A means one, the indefinite article
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes police detectives
the head is the top of something

explanation.surface: A senior police detective turns out to take drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top detective' looks like a chief inspector, but split it: the pieces go into the answer in the order one, detective, top.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidhead is slang for a habitual taker of LSD, the drug known as acid.

clue.text: Statutory steps taken for health provision

explanation.definitionFit: Constitutional means laid down by law, like an established rule; it is also a brisk walk taken for one's health.

clue.text: This girl wasn't well brought up

indicators.note: in a down light, brought up means the word for wasn't well is read from bottom to top

parts.note: someone who wasn't well ailed

explanation.surface: A girl who had a sickly childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' looks like upbringing; in a down clue it turns AILED upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Exotic drama we are mounting? Butler did it!

indicators.note: in a down light, mounting means the whole run of letters climbs, read upward

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese theatre, exotic to Western eyes
we are in the past tense gives were

explanation.surface: A whodunit joke: the butler did it, said of a foreign stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butler did it' is the stock detective-story ending, but Samuel Butler is the Victorian novelist who wrote this satire. 'mounting' reverses NOH + WERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Butler wrote the satirical novel of that title, an imaginary country whose name is nowhere spelt roughly backwards.

clue.text: Giving a tonic, perhaps, as encouragement to choir

explanation.definitionFit: Dosing is administering medicine such as a tonic; and a choirmaster urging singers might say do sing.

clue.text: For whom right and wrong can go in ledger

definitions.text: For whom right and wrong can go in ledger

indicators.note: wrong signals that the following words are put into a wrong, scrambled order

explanation.surface: Someone who notes down good and bad deeds in an account book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges CAN GO IN LEDGER into ECORDINGANGEL, placed after R. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian tradition a heavenly scribe keeps a register of each person's good and evil acts.

clue.text: Like Labour programme, highly taxing

explanation.definitionFit: Hercules performed twelve legendary labours, so the word describes enormous effort; it also means extremely demanding.

clue.text: City having top players, you might say

indicators.note: you might say signals a word that sounds like the one meant

parts.note: the leads are the principal actors, the top players in a cast

explanation.surface: A city whose football or theatre stars are the best.
explanation.walkthrough: LEADS spoken sounds like the Yorkshire city LEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire, northern England.

clue.text: Drive off with a politician inside for a wash

indicators.note: inside says the second pieces go within the word for drive off

parts.note: shoo means to drive away, as with a cat
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone chases away a politician who has come in to wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive off' looks like leaving in a car, but it means scaring something away; 'inside' puts the article and the politician inside that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shampoo is a wash of the hair or a carpet.

clue.text: Can include a head in informal conference

indicators.note: include says the word for can holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a can is a tin
a head, as in pricing per head, means each

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a leader may be invited to a casual meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb asking permission, but it is the metal container; 'include' puts 'a head' (per person) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an informal session of lectures and discussion on a topical issue.

clue.text: Binding volume with a cover

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A book with its binding and a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Binding' and 'volume' suggest bookbinding, but Binding is the definition, in its legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A valid contract is legally binding, enforceable in law.

clue.text: Lots of information returned at short notice to bench

indicators.note: returned says both of the first two pieces come back in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
an ad is a notice, short for advertisement
a bank is a bench, such as a row of seats for oarsmen

explanation.surface: Information brought back to a judge's bench at short notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses both 'at' and the short notice, which gives DATA.
explanation.definitionFit: A databank is a large store of information, usually computerised.

clue.text: Shoot at foreign female — it's only a game

parts.note: to bag is to shoot game
taken as written
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: Someone fires at a foreign woman and shrugs it off as play.
explanation.walkthrough: ELLE is French for she, hence 'foreign female'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game of rolling balls into scoring holes; the word also means a trifle.

clue.text: Way in which poet goes after fish

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
Thomas Gray was the English poet of the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

explanation.surface: A route along which a poet goes fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAY is Thomas Gray, the 18th-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat fish with a venomous spine on its tail.

clue.text: Don't fall, say, for temporary attachment?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, sounding like the answer

parts.note: a warning not to fall is slip not

explanation.surface: A warning against falling, given while securing something only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIP NOT spoken sounds like SLIPKNOT, since the K is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipknot can be undone with a pull, so it is a temporary fastening.

clue.text: Pick up cricket side and leave the ground

parts.note: to pick up is to lift
the off side is one half of a cricket field, the side facing the batsman

explanation.surface: Collecting a cricket team before taking flight.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the OFF side is the half of the field in front of a batsman as they stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift-off is the moment an aircraft or rocket rises into the air.

clue.text: Union leader's funding

explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S. Grant commanded the Northern armies in the American Civil War; a grant is also money awarded.

clue.text: Finished everywhere, typically

explanation.definitionFit: All over can mean ended, or throughout a place, or characteristic of someone, as in that's him all over.

clue.text: Potential customers gather round head of department

indicators.note: round says the word for gather goes around the other letter

parts.note: to amass is to gather together

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of department

explanation.surface: Shoppers crowd around a store's departmental boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gather round' reads as one phrase; split it, with AMASS placed round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Admass is the mass public targeted by advertising.

clue.text: Composer's manual, so to speak

parts.note: manual spoken sounds like the Spanish given name of a composer whose surname is wanted

explanation.surface: A handbook written by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Manuel de Falla was a Spanish composer; 'manual' spoken sounds like his first name, so the answer is the rest of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish composer of The Three-Cornered Hat was named Manuel, which sounds like manual.

clue.text: Some Europeans reported services out of order

indicators.note: reported signals that the word is spoken, sounding like the answer

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and must be replayed, an invalid service

explanation.surface: Church services cancelled, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: LETS spoken sounds like LETTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Letts is a name for Latvians, people of a Baltic country.

clue.text: Flier's daughter to take off or to land

indicators.note: to take off says a letter is removed from the following words

parts.note: taken as written; the answer runs through these words only because removing the daughter leaves it, a coincidence of the deletion and not a hidden word

explanation.surface: A pilot's daughter must choose between departing and touching down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' and 'land' paint a flight, but 'to take off' removes D from OR TO LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European bunting, a bird.

clue.text: A short distance up

explanation.definitionFit: Twelve inches is a short span; afoot also means astir, in motion, as plans are underway.

clue.text: Stick with large version always

indicators.note: version signals a different form, a rearrangement of the word large

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: Sticking with a bigger edition for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges LARGE into GEARL, followed by EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gear stick is the lever in a car for changing gear.

clue.text: It's not hard to attract business

definitions.text: It's not hard to attract business

parts.words: It's not hard to attract business
parts.note: reads as saying drawing in trade is easy, but means a gentle, unpressured approach to selling

explanation.surface: Winning customers is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' looks like easy, but means gentle as opposed to hard-sell.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-pressure persuasive sales technique is the opposite of aggressive salesmanship.

clue.text: Sporting type, but not blue

explanation.definitionFit: A hearty is a boisterous sporty person, especially at university; hearty also means cheerful, not depressed.
